title: How Zach Yadegari went from a school unblocked-games site to Cal AI and viral iOS apps
summary: Zach tells how he grew Totally Science to 5M users via classroom TikTok videos, sold it on Flippa, then moved to iOS apps. He covers revamping Grind Clock into a subscription app, launching Cal AI with organic TikTok, why he avoids raising capital, and building in-house tools.

principles.text: Spot a fragmented behavior and consolidate it into one hub; Totally Science combined scattered game sites.
principles.quote: I identified the opportunity to combine all of these games on different websites under one website which acted as a hub and that was totally science

principles.text: Market via self-made social content showing the product in its real context, not paid ads.
principles.quote: I created content myself just recording myself in class playing on the website and I attained a few million views from the videos I posted

principles.text: Revisit apps that still get organic downloads; revamp them and switch to subscriptions.
principles.quote: we saw clearly people liked the app we could say that was probably attributed partially to the Tik Tok video still getting some views

principles.text: Not raising capital forces profitability and urgency from day one.
principles.quote: not having Capital raised puts a fire under you that forces is you to make it work and one it needs to be profitable from the start

principles.text: Take incumbent apps' necessary features and make them easier with AI; prove accuracy with a test bench.
principles.quote: first we took all the features that were necessary and we made them easier with AI now we're going to take all the features that are useful and make those easier with AI as well

principles.text: Build in-house testing tools to move fast and reuse them across future apps, like app studios do.
principles.quote: we will be able to repurpose them with future apps so we will be able to just easily put our foot in the door in a new industry
